subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should a durable wake remain owned by the canonical session key across a session reset, or must delivery be fenced to the session generation that created the wake, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559 be the sole canonical branch?
rationale: Both semantics are implementable, but they produce different session-state and message-routing guarantees; repository policy and tests do not establish which behavior maintainers intend for the new durable runtime.

options.title: Fence and consolidate
options.body: Require generation-aware wake delivery or explicit supersession on mismatch, carry the change and proof only in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559, then close this predecessor.

options.title: Approve key-scoped delivery
options.body: Explicitly approve wakes following the canonical session key across resets, document that contract, and add focused reset-boundary proof to the canonical PR.

options.title: Pause durable core
options.body: Keep the stack unmerged until maintainers choose a narrower durable-runtime architecture and sequencing plan.

recommendation.title: Fence and consolidate
recommendation.body: Require generation-aware wake delivery or explicit supersession on mismatch, carry the change and proof only in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559, then close this predecessor.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a new core runtime and session-ownership contract whose acceptance depends on repository-wide product direction rather than a mechanical repair.
